title: Auditable Human-Agent Teams for Autonomous X-ray Experimentation
abstract: arXiv:2611.12933v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Closed-loop autonomous experimentation can accelerate scientific discovery, but implementation effort limits accessibility. Agentic systems may lower this barrier, although sustained operation on physical instruments remains largely unexplored. Here, using coding-agent infrastructure grounded in validated scientific methods, we demonstrate autonomous synchrotron X-ray experiments on nanoparticle superlattices under evolving, human-defined objectives. Complete human-agent and agent-agent transcripts enable an audit that reconstructs decision provenance and characterizes the division of cognitive labor. Across three experiments, 61-67% of messages involved interpretation or judgment, while the share of methodological and scientific contributions increased from 46% in the setup-focused first experiment to 56-61% in later experiments. tldr: 该研究利用可审计的人-智能体协作团队在真实同步辐射装置上实现了纳米粒子超晶格的自主X射线实验，并通过完整对话记录审计决策溯源与认知分工，证明智能体系统能够在物理仪器上持续运行并逐步承担更多科学贡献。
en_tdlr: This work demonstrates autonomous synchrotron X-ray experiments on nanoparticle superlattices using auditable human-agent teams, whose complete transcripts enable reconstruction of decision provenance and characterization of cognitive labor division, showing that agentic systems can sustain operation on physical instruments while progressively taking on greater scientific contributions.
